VAN.head: The Canucks face a real test
VAN.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, Philadelphia has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ best way through is getting good looks.

PHI.head: The matchup suits the Flyers
PHI.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, Philadelphia has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Canucks are on a four-game losing streak, and the Flyers (4-10-4) lost 3-2 to the Rangers on Thursday. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. The Flyers played last night, and the Canucks are rested. Going in, the Flyers are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Flyers haven’t played well, but their record (.333) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .387, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Canucks (.194 on chances worth .323), mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games.

The Flyers block more shots than almost anyone (3rd), but get a lot of their shots blocked (30th). Philadelphia has scored 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. On the other side, the Canucks pick their shots (lowest), have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (32nd). Vancouver has allowed 4.61 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 18 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Matvei Michkov (10 G / 3 A / 13 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for tenth in the NHL. For the Canucks, Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brock Boeser (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 18 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Joseph Woll (1-6-2 / .898 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Philadelphia, and Leevi Meriläinen (2-6-1 / .889 SV% in 10 GS) for Vancouver.
At home, Manny Malhotra likes to send Cotter, Sasson and Gallagher out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Barkey, Couturier and Acciari.

items.text: The Flyers have been without Rasmus Ristolainen since Oct 24, and have had to make do without Nikita Grebenkin all season.
The Canucks are newly without Filip Chytil and Tom Willander, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Matvei Michkov has ten goals on chances worth about 5.1 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Sean Couturier is two assists from passing Rod Brind'Amour for ninth on the Flyers’ all-time assists list.
